Verdict: BENIGN

Identification
  github.com/Elementsproject/elements@v0.3.12 is an archive of historical
  Bitcoin client C++ source: wxWidgets wallet UI, transaction/block validation,
  peer networking, proof-of-work generation, and a local JSON-RPC interface.
  Sample SHA256:
  8b1fb167da2eb531fdecde25bb3f24a8fef2a8ba96d318290404ebf83a303b46

Earlier release and decisive diff
  Fetched https://proxy.golang.org/github.com/!elementsproject/elements/@v/v0.3.10.zip
  Earlier archive SHA256:
  c7a3c4243bc13898fac5d843b4125091d373a81680be506932ec196d1afc7d0d
  The earlier archive has CRLF lines; normalize them before comparing.
  Neither archive adds or removes members relative to the other. The full
  normalized diff is 3517 lines, comprising 21 changed source/build files.

  ui.cpp's GetAutostartDir through the Linux SetStartOnSystemStartup body is
  IDENTICAL after line-ending normalization. SHA256 of that source region:
  7b867282327157363d2ab18978bf07687839f6ae42431d1b3ca420bfed025016
  The ui.cpp changes concern warning/status text and removal of obsolete
  socket-thread monitoring, not the startup code.

  At ui.cpp:1554-1556, !fAutoStart deletes
  GetAutostartFilePath().native_file_string().c_str(). That helper resolves
  bitcoin.desktop under XDG_CONFIG_HOME/autostart or HOME/.config/autostart.
  The mutually exclusive enabled branch at 1558-1580 reads /proc/self/exe
  into pszExePath, then WRITES that path to the desktop entry's Exec field.
  unlink never receives pszExePath. The options dialog calls the setter when
  its startup checkbox changes (1737-1740); first-run initialization also
  enables the option (init.cpp:401). This is normal autostart management.

  With this checkout's pre-edit rules, v0.3.10 ALSO fires the same suspicious
  self-delete composite. Thus the queue's clean earlier baseline does not
  reproduce with the present rule set. The new-version premise cannot
  establish a compromise when the flagged implementation is unchanged.

Other changed execution paths reviewed
  - db.cpp adds BackupWallet, reached from rpc.cpp's backupwallet method.
    It flushes the owned wallet database and copies wallet.dat to the caller's
    destination path. RPC binds 127.0.0.1:8332, checks the peer, and verifies
    configured Basic authentication before dispatch. No remote upload sink.
  - main.h adds money-range and proof-of-work checks; main.cpp checks input
    totals, fees, block size, and signature-operation limits. script.cpp adds
    limits and disables risky arithmetic/string opcodes. These harden the
    transaction interpreter, rather than invoking an OS command interpreter.
  - main.cpp's new alert handler calls CAlert::ProcessAlert; main.h:1676
    verifies the message against a fixed public key BEFORE deserializing its
    unsigned contents. Accepted alerts update warnings/RPC safe mode and are
    relayed to peers. No arbitrary command, download, or code execution sink.
  - IRC NICK/USER/JOIN/WHO discover Bitcoin peers. Received JOIN/WHO nicknames
    are Base58-decoded into network addresses and passed to AddAddress.
    The release diff adds exception handling and buffer reservation, not C2
    dispatch. HTTP external-IP discovery and peer traffic serve node operation.
  - Long hex strings include genesis transaction bytes and public keys; Base58
    encodes Bitcoin addresses, and Base64 supports RPC Basic authentication.
    There is no concealed executable payload. ASCII XPM pixels yielded
    accidental UTF-16 Hangul in extracted text, not Korean program content.

Trait corrections
  - Self-delete now requires adjacent readlink and unlink statements sharing
    the same captured buffer, with /proc/self/exe as the readlink source.
    Mere proximity and unrelated temp/mount exclusions no longer decide it.
  - Native socket binding requires a sockaddr cast or assembly API invocation;
    Boost callback binding is not a socket bind. Source listener consumers
    reference that evidence; the POSIX binary symbol rule stays binary-only.
  - Windows KTM source commits require one argument; Bitcoin's two-argument
    CommitTransaction is different. GetFileSize stays case-sensitive so the
    local GetFilesize wrapper is not treated as the Windows API. Native file
    remove excludes std::remove's three-argument collection operation.
  - Native write requires a free three-argument call; two-argument C++ stream
    methods do not establish POSIX write. The looped-write pattern also requires
    a third argument and cannot cross a closing parenthesis to invent one.
  - Coinbase wallet references require wallet wording or coinbase.com; a
    protocol coinbase transaction is not that product. Meet-in-the-middle
    requires attack wording, excluding the peer-subscription routing comment.
  - Recognized XPM source headers exclude accidental pixel-text Hangul.
    OpenSSL acknowledgements remain notable license-attribution observations,
    without establishing that UI credits or build documentation are OpenSSL.
  - Generic IRC commands, IP endpoints, XOR arithmetic, native export lookup,
    ShowWindow, literal-length measurements, and Bitcoin script representation
    references have neutral homes. Consumers are updated in moved-ids.json.
  - The two equivalent Python XOR spellings share one structured operation
    rule, excluding quoted code. A PHP chr(ord(...)) conversion was moved out
    of arithmetic and renamed: its matcher proves neither XOR nor a loop.
    These consolidations keep directory budgets intact without an overflow
    bucket or hiding a finding at a lower severity.

Verification
  atomscan and cleave facts were run on the sample; ui.cpp facts and the
  matched source paths were inspected. Scans explicitly used this checkout
  through CLEAVE_TRAITS_DIR, with automatic updates disabled.
  Final archive scan: zero hostile traits, zero suspicious traits; 125 unique
  notable traits remain on analyzed members, including real networking,
  cryptography, file operations, and autostart configuration.
  check.py exercises self-deletion positives with renamed buffers; unrelated
  deletion targets, overwrite and autostart negatives; real/overloaded APIs;
  attribution; arithmetic; export lookup; actual Korean versus XPM pixels;
  Python XOR operations versus quoted code; and native versus stream writes.
  make validate is the final repository gate.
